result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B's Home screen puts a real search field at the top, with items due soon, holds ready for pickup and today's hours right below it. That covers the library's core jobs in one tap, and its zero-results fallback is more layered, including cross-search into events and branches. A is very thorough on what the app remembers and on My Items behaviors like renew and undo, but its landing screen is just the Search tab, with no status summary. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put a visible search field up front and handle typing and empty results well. A is stronger on finding matches outside the catalog and on fallback content when a search turns up nothing. B wins because it makes the core tasks concrete: Renew and Renew all on each row, holds ready for pickup listed first, and today's hours shown on the branch screen. B also says more about what the app remembers, including the card number, pickup branch, home branch, filters and scroll position.
